question.worked_solution:
The statement $A⇒B$ is true *unless* $A$ is true and $B$ is false. 

Let's break this down into cases:

- When $A=\text{F}$ and $B=\text{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(A⇒B) & ≡(\text{F}⇒\text{T}) \\  & ≡\text{T}.\end{aligned}
$$

- When $A=\text{F}$ and $B=\text{F},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(A⇒B) & ≡(\text{F}⇒\text{F}) \\  & ≡\text{T}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $A$ is false, then $A⇒B$ is $\text{always true}.$

The complete truth table for $A⇒B$ is shown below:

| $\,A\,$ | $\,B\,$ | $\,A⇒B\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{T}$ | $\text{F}$ | $F$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ | $\text{T}$ |
| $\text{F}$ | $\text{F}$ | $\text{T}$ |
